Match items of List-I with those of List-II :

  
    
    List - I
(Property)
    
    List - II
(Example)
  

  
    (a)
    Diamagnetism
    (i)
    MnO
  
  
    (b)
    Ferrimagnetism
    (ii)
    $O_{2}$
  
  
    (c)
    Paramagnetism
    (iii)
    NaCl
  
  
    (d)
    Antiferromagnetism
    (iv)
    $Fe_{3}O_{4}$
  

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A. NaCl is diamagnetic because all electrons are paired in $Na^{+}$ and in $Cl^{−}$ . So, it shows diamagnetism. 

 $B. Fe_{3}O_{4}$ is ferrimagnetic because of the presence of the unequal alignment of magnetic moment in opposite direction. 

 $C. O_{2}$ molecule has two unpaired electrons. So, it is paramagnetic. 

 D. In MnO, the orientation of the electrons of Mn and O is such that they cancel their effects, hence it is antiferromagnetic.

text: Acidic ferric chloride solution on treatment with excess of potassium ferrocyanide gives a Prussian blue coloured colloidal species. It is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Prussian blue is iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), formed when $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ions meet $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$ ions.

With excess potassium ferrocyanide, each $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ combines with one $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$, and the remaining charge is balanced by $\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$:

$\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}\qquad +\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]\longrightarrow \mathrm{KFe}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]+3\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$

$\mathrm{KFe}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ is the soluble form of Prussian blue and remains as a colloidal dispersion; the insoluble $\mathrm{Fe}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}_{3}$ precipitates only when $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is in excess.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text:
In Carius method for estimation of halogens, 0.2 g of an organic compound gave 0.188 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine in the compound is $______________. ($Nearest integer)

solution.body:

If the rate of appearance of $Cr_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}$ is 2.67 mol $\min ^{-1}$ at a particular time, the rate of disappearance of $C_{2}H_{6}O$ at the same time is $_____________$ mol $\min ^{-1}. ($Nearest integer)

text:
1 kg of 0.75 molal aqueous solution of sucrose can be cooled up to $-$4${}^{\circ }$C before freezing. The amount of ice (in g) that will be separated out is $__________. ($Nearest integer)

[Given : $K_{f}(H_{2}O) = 1.86 K kg$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The molar mass of sucrose, $\mathrm{C}{}_{12}\mathrm{H}{}_{22}\mathrm{O}{}_{11}$, is $342\text{g mol}^{-1}$. Let the 1000 g of solution contain $w$ g of water and $n$ mol of sucrose.

Molality gives $\dfrac{n}{w/1000}=0.75$, so $n=7.5\times 10^{-4}w$; the total mass gives $w+342n=1000$.

$w(1+0.2565)=1000\Rightarrow w=795.9\text{g},n=0.5969\text{mol}$

On cooling, only pure water separates as ice and all the sucrose stays in the remaining liquid. At $-4{}^{\circ }\text{C}$, $\Delta T_{f}=4\text{K}$, so the water left in the solution, $w^{'}$, satisfies

$4=1.86\times \dfrac{0.5969}{w^{'}}\Rightarrow w^{'}=0.2776\text{kg}=277.6\text{g}$

Ice separated $=795.9-277.6=518.3\text{g}\approx 518\text{g}$.

Hence, the answer is 518.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: 1 mol of an octahedral metal complex with formula MCl$_{3} . 2L$ on reaction with excess of AgNO$_{3}$ gives 1 mol of AgCl. The denticity of Ligand L is $____________. ($Integer answer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
One mole of the complex gives 1 mol of AgCl with excess $\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}$, so only one $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is outside the coordination sphere and the other two $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ are bonded to M. The complex is $[\mathrm{MCl}{}_{2}\mathrm{L}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}$.

An octahedral complex has coordination number 6. The two $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ occupy 2 positions, so the two L ligands fill the remaining 4 positions:

$2+2\times (\text{denticity of L})=6\Rightarrow \text{denticity of L}=2$

L is a bidentate ligand.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: The number of moles of CuO, that will be utilized in Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen in a sample of 57.5 g of N, N-dimethylaminopentane is $_____________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Moles of N in N, N - dimethylaminopentane = $\left (\frac{57.5}{115}\right )$ = 0.5 mol

$\Rightarrow C_{7}H_{17}N+\frac{45}{2}CuO\to 7CO_{2}+\frac{17}{2}H_{2}O+\frac{1}{2}N_{2}+\frac{45}{2}Cu$

$\frac{n_{CuO}reacted}{\left (\frac{45}{2}\right )}=\frac{n_{C7H17N}reacted}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $n_{$CuO} reacted = $\left (\frac{45}{2}\right )\times 0.5=11.25$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: The number of f electrons in the ground state electronic configuration of Np (Z = 93) is $___________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ground-state configuration of Np $(Z=93)$ is

$[\text{Rn}]5f^{4}6d^{1}7s^{2},[\text{Rn}]=[\text{Xe}]4f^{14}5d^{10}6s^{2}6p^{6}$

The Xe core ($1s$ to $5p$) has no f electrons, so the occupied f subshells are $4f$ with 14 electrons and $5f$ with 4 electrons.

Number of f electrons $=14+4=18$

Hence, the answer is 18.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text:
200 mL of 0.2 M HCl is mixed with 300 mL of 0.1 M NaOH. The molar heat of neutralization of this reaction is $-$57.1 kJ. The increase in temperature in ${}^{\circ }$C of the system on mixing is x $\times$ $10^{-2}$. The value of x is $___________. ($Nearest integer)

[Given : Specific heat of water $= 4.18 J g^{-1} K^{-1}$, Density of water $= 1.00 g cm^{-3}$]

[Assume no volume change on mixing]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Rightarrow$ Millimoles of HCl = 200 $\times$ 0.2 = 40

$\Rightarrow$ Millimoles of NaOH = 300 $\times$ 0.1 = 30

$\Rightarrow$ Heat released = $\left (\frac{30}{1000}\times 57.1\times 1000\right )$ = 1713 J

$\Rightarrow$ Mass of solution = 500 ml $\times$ 1 gm/ml = 500 gm

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta T=\frac{q}{m\times c}=\frac{1713J}{500g\times 4.18\frac{J}{g-K}}$ = 0.8196 K

= 81.96 $\times$ $10^{-2} K$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift
